title: How Much Tree Closes a Dome
hook: One dome, every triangle closed with wedges: four trees, or seven, and you choose which.

source.title: Wedge strut footage and triangle infill for the 2V wedge dome
source.transcript_file: the owner's chat; every figure re-derived and checked in two_v_demo/wedge_coverage_facts.py (22 of 22 agree with the dome solver)
source.note: Not a video: a worked analysis. Its numbers are recomputed from the dome's own geometry here; the card only sets the choices the analysis made.

summary: The dome's frame is {dome_members} wedge members: {frame_ft} feet of wedge, cut from one log after another. Close every triangle with more wedges, laid in pairs with their points facing in, and the pairs can nest tight or open into a bowtie. Nested, a pair covers one wedge face; opened, two. That one choice moves the whole dome between {total_min_ft} and {total_max_ft} feet of wedge.

numbers.name: log_in
numbers.label: log diameter
numbers.source: the owner's working assumption in the ChatGPT session (a chat, not a video, so no timestamp): the owner's working assumption in the session: a 12 in pine

numbers.name: splits
numbers.label: wedges per log section

numbers.name: tree_ft
numbers.label: one usable pine
numbers.source: the owner's working assumption in the ChatGPT session (a chat, not a video, so no timestamp): the owner, in the session: 'given a 60 foot tree, that's 10 chunks x 8 wedges'

numbers.name: overlap_open

numbers.why: the least wood; a real joint needs some overlap

beats.title: The frame
beats.narration: A {log_in} inch log split {splits} ways gives wedges with a face {face_in} inches wide. The frame takes {dome_members} of them, {frame_ft} feet of wedge, and one {tree_ft} foot pine gives {tree_wedge_ft} feet.

beats.title: Closing the triangles
beats.narration: The triangles leave {dome_open_sqft_12in} square feet to close after the frame. Lay the wedges in pairs, points facing in. Nested tight, a pair covers one face; opened to a bowtie, two.

beats.title: Your choice of trees
beats.narration: Bowtie pairs close the dome with {infill_min_ft} feet of infill; nested pairs take {infill_max_ft}. Frame and all, that is {total_min_ft} to {total_max_ft} feet: {trees_min} to {trees_max} trees, before taper and kerf.

dome_fit.narration: This is the whole timber bill of the wedge dome closed in wood: {total_min_ft} to {total_max_ft} feet of wedge against a frame of {frame_ft}.

limits.narration: A bowtie touches only at its points: the {infill_min_ft} foot figure is a floor, not a weather-tight joint. And the area method runs about six per cent above the real pieces the Triangle Infill calculator cuts, because a triangle's corners take short pieces.
